gaps.title: A 'verified' verdict checks the predicate, not the claim's text
gaps.case: /tmp/claude-0/probes/p1.ts at 9373f4d: claim text 'app.js does NOT use eval and is safe' with predicate file.contains {text:'eval'} -> verified; text 'app.js has no network endpoints' with file.contains {text:'a'} -> verified. src/verifier/verifier.ts:91-136 never relates text to predicate; the M4 corpus (test/verifier.test.ts:21-23) sets text to the predicate string, so it cannot catch this.
gaps.impact: The UI shows a check mark next to agent-written text that the evidence does not support, including negations; calibration counts these as correct.
gaps.fix: Render the verdict on a statement generated from predicate+params and show it instead of, or beside, the agent text; add mismatched and negated claims to the M4 corpus with a false-verified-as-read target of 0.

gaps.title: M12 grades the two arms on different text and with different prompts
gaps.case: bench/live.ts:107 grades Tier 0 on its answer; :149-152 grades Assay on answer plus every claim's text and JSON params. Prompts differ (:86 asks Tier 0 to cite file and offset; :122 does not). Recomputing bench/results/live.json on answers only gives Assay 88/105 vs Tier 0 90/105. Grader is substring match (:49-58) with keys such as 'pe', 'elf', 'zip', 'install', 'https'. Harness reads a skill from a hard-coded local path (:27). The bootstrap resamples 24 cells from 8 tasks.
gaps.impact: README:94-100 'as accurate ... about 43% cheaper' is not supported as stated; part of the cost gap may come from the longer Tier 0 prompt.
gaps.fix: Same prompt for both arms, answer-only grading with token-boundary matching, vendored skill text, task-level bootstrap, 60 paired cells as docs/debt.md already requires.

gaps.title: CLI --json output is silently truncated at 64 KiB when piped
gaps.case: `node src/cli.ts sweep . --json --home <tmp> | wc -c` returned 65536 in three runs; redirected to a file the same report is 558,664 bytes; exit status 0. src/cli.ts:217 calls process.exit(code) before stdout drains.
gaps.impact: Agents and scripts that pipe JSON get invalid, truncated JSON with a success exit code.
gaps.fix: Set process.exitCode and return, or write with a drained callback; add a CI test that pipes a large --json result and parses it.

gaps.title: cmd.exit re-runs inherit the full environment and store output unredacted
gaps.case: /tmp/claude-0/probes/p3.ts: an approved cmd.exit claim whose command prints a token-shaped environment value -> evidence volatile.stdout_tail holds it verbatim (redactString would have flagged it). src/app/app.ts:144 passes no env to runProcess (assay_exec uses execEnv, src/mcp/tools.ts:307-317); app.ts:163 stores stdout_tail without redact; bundles include volatile (src/export/export.ts:196).
gaps.impact: Secrets reach the store, the UI and shareable bundles, contradicting README:56.
gaps.fix: Use execEnv() for verifier commands and pass stdout_tail through redactString; add a regression test with a planted token.

gaps.title: .git write protection checks only the lexical path
gaps.case: /tmp/claude-0/probes/p1.ts against the 9373f4d tree: resolveInWorkspace(ws, 'docs/hooks/pre-commit', {write:true}) with docs -> .git resolves to <ws>/.git/hooks/pre-commit and is allowed; '.GIT/hooks/pre-commit' is allowed (on case-insensitive macOS/Windows file systems this is .git). src/mcp/paths.ts:33 tests segments of the lexical relative path.
gaps.impact: An approved assay_write_file can plant a git hook while the approval shows an innocuous path; target repositories are attacker-controlled and may ship such a symlink.
gaps.fix: Apply the protected-segment test to the realpath relative to the root, case-insensitively on darwin/win32; add symlink and case tests on ubuntu and macOS.

gaps.title: Bundle verification trusts the bundle's own key by default
gaps.case: /tmp/claude-0/probes/p2.ts: a bundle whose claim verdicts were flipped to 'verified' and re-signed with a fresh Ed25519 key passes verifyBundle() without a key; `assay verify --bundle` (src/cli.ts:148-160) then prints 'bundle verifies'. src/export/export.ts:232 falls back to b.signature.public_key.
gaps.impact: README:61 'signed bundles that anyone can check' reads as origin assurance; without a trusted key the check proves only self-consistency. Bundle claims also omit predicate and params (export.ts:196-202).
gaps.fix: Require --key or a local trust store, print 'untrusted signer' and exit non-zero otherwise; include predicate and params in manifest claims.

gaps.title: Effect declarations understate two worker tools
gaps.case: assay_release_worker is declared effect 'none' (src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts:901-910), so tools/list marks it readOnlyHint true (src/mcp/server.ts:57-67), yet it runs `git worktree remove --force` (src/orchestrator/worktree.ts:44). assay_reply_worker (orchestrator.ts:886) is 'none' and starts a paid model turn; spawn is always allowed (src/policy/taint.ts:156).
gaps.impact: Clients and people relying on MCP hints treat a destructive, ungated action as read-only; a tainted coordinator can discard a worker's uncommitted work without approval.
gaps.fix: Declare release as write (approval when the worktree is dirty) and reply/spawn with their cost; test the hints against handler behaviour.

gaps.title: Approvals show at most 2,000 characters of each argument
gaps.case: src/mcp/registry.ts:145-152 summarizeArgs cuts strings over 2,000 characters before ctx.approve; assay_write_file accepts up to 10 MiB (src/mcp/tools.ts:37).
gaps.impact: The person approves file content they cannot see; a payload after character 2,000 is written unseen.
gaps.fix: Show size and digest, keep full content behind a handle the UI can open, and refuse approval rendering that hides content without saying so.

gaps.title: Worker reports reach the coordinator outside the untrusted envelope
gaps.case: assay_check_workers (src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts:867-884) returns worker summaries and questions as plain text with no untrusted flag, so registry.shape() neither envelopes them nor taints the coordinator.
gaps.impact: Instructions a worker copied from target content arrive at the coordinator as trusted text; approval reasons omit 'session read untrusted content'.
gaps.fix: Mark worker-originated text untrusted with origin worker:<id>, and propagate taint from worker to coordinator.

gaps.title: Budget cap is checked against past spend only; workers have no session cap
gaps.case: orchestrator.ts:218 and :612 call checkBudget with {calls: 1}; the USD of the coming turn is not estimated against the limit. Worker runners get no maxBudgetUsd (orchestrator.ts:655-660). docs/configuration.md:14 says a turn or worker that would cross the cap is refused.
gaps.impact: A case can exceed its USD cap by one coordinator turn plus every running worker turn.
gaps.fix: Pass remaining budget as maxBudgetUsd to every session, and refuse spawns when the estimate's upper bound crosses the cap.

gaps.title: CI at the reviewed commit is red and Windows has never passed
gaps.case: Run 40243131708 on 9373f4d: check job failed at 'npm run lint', so coverage, docs freshness, SBOM, install rehearsal, e2e, benchmark gates and self-application were skipped; macos-14 passed; windows-2022 npm test still running after >10 min (macOS takes ~45 s). Run 40240963852 windows job cancelled at the 30-min timeout. Commit a5fbe8a (after HEAD) names a pty leak that kept npm test alive on Windows.
gaps.impact: README:69 'runs in CI' and the workflow's 'Tests also run on macOS and Windows' describe gates that did not pass at this commit.
gaps.fix: Keep a required green check on the branch; add a per-test timeout on Windows; state the supported OS matrix in support.json.

gaps.title: README and configuration docs drifted from results and code
gaps.case: README.md:74-75 reports M2 7,565 B and M3 median 777 B; bench/results/latest.md at the same commit reports 7,952 B and 545.5 B. docs/configuration.md:15 documents auto-approval rules 'per case (approvals API)', but no route or UI calls ApprovalQueue.addRule (git grep: only tests).

questions: Does loopback auth hold (Host/Origin, pairing, cookies, WS tickets, MCP bearer tokens)? Yes for remote and browser callers; tokens are per case and caller, digests only.
Do path guards hold? Workspace containment yes (realpath); .git write protection no (symlink and case variants).
Can a claim be marked verified wrongly? Yes: the verdict covers predicate+params, not the agent's text.
Do durability tests test what they claim? The kernel mechanics yes (real SIGKILLs, real second process); the product's orchestrator and sweep are not fault-injected.
